prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. NEW seamless terrain texture atlas for a monochrome Pokemon-style top down JRPG, coarse logical32x32 tiles. Exactly4 columns and4 rows, sixteen square cells filling entire square image, no gutters, frames, margins, labels or grid lines. Each cell is a FULL BLEED ground SURFACE, no isolated objects, no white backdrop. Black and white only with chunky ordered dithering. Texture extends through every edge, repeats seamlessly, consistent pattern phase and scale. No props, buildings, mushrooms, rocks as objects, creatures or perspective. Flat top-down ground textures.
Row1 four textures: mottled dry meadow grass medium density; light compacted dirt with small scattered grain flecks, still visibly textured across whole tile; dense grainfield stubble with short stalk strokes; dark furrowed soil.
Row2: moss carpet with tiny leaf curls; light forest soil speckled with leaf litter; dark pond water with broken white horizontal ripples; dense wet reeds and moss texture.
Row3: shell-speckled sand medium density; light packed shore sand with tiny broken wavy lines; dark sea water with white wavelets; densely layered reef bed texture.
Row4: mottled ash and gravel medium density; lighter quarry floor with small grit and hairline fissures; dark coal seam with tiny white cracks; dense flinty fractured stone.
Light walking surface texture should have about15-20 percent black coverage, base surface35percent, dark patches60percent; recognizable contrasting materials with no blank tile. Hard pixel clusters and heavy checkerboard dithering, not photoreal, no grayscale gradients, no borders. Design surfaces to mesh into a connected world rather than separate stamps on paper.
